State Law reference— Local inspectors and inspections for building code enforcement purposes, O.C.G.A. § 8-2-26; right of certain fire officials and delegees to enter for purposes of inspection, O.C.G.A. § 25-2-22.
902:
The inspection and examination authorized by this article shall be for the purpose of reporting and correcting the following fire hazards pertaining to buildings and the occupants:
(1) Disrepair.
(2) Age and dilapidated condition.
(3) Faulty or unapproved construction.
(4) Inadequate fire escapes or lack of means of egress.
(5) Inadequate fire alarm protection.
(6) Inadequate fire extinguishing equipment.
(7) Materials and buildings especially susceptible to fire.
(8) Conditions endangering other property or occupants.
(9) Any other fire hazards dangerous to life or property.
(Code 1999, § 3-703; Code 2011, § 24-24)
904:
Where violations of this chapter or of any other laws or ordinances relating to fire hazards are found by the fire chief or his designee, he shall serve a written order to correct the violation upon the owner, operator, occupant, or other person responsible for the violation.
(1) Method of service. The order required herein shall be served in one of the following ways:
a. By making personal delivery of the order to the person responsible.
b. By leaving the order with some person of suitable age and discretion upon the premises.
c. By affixing a copy of the order to the door at the entrance of the premises in violation.
(2) Time for compliance. The order required herein shall set forth a time limit for compliance, dependent upon the hazard and danger created by the violation. In cases of extreme danger to persons or property, immediate compliance upon service of the order may be required.
(3) Appeal from order. A person to whom an order hereunder is directed shall have the right, within 24 hours of the service of such order, to appeal to the council, who shall review such order within ten days and file its decision thereon. Unless the order is revoked or modified, it shall remain in full force and be obeyed by the person to whom directed. No person to whom an order is directed shall fail to comply with such order within ten days after an appeal shall have been determined.
(4) Failure to comply. When a person to whom an order is directed shall fail to comply within the specified time, the fire chief shall have the authority to contract with others for the removal of such materials and charge the cost thereof to the person to whom the order is directed. The person removing material under a contract made hereunder shall be authorized to enter the premises and to remove such material.
(5) Failure to pay costs of removal. If the cost of removal is not paid within ten days after receipt of a statement therefor from the city clerk, such cost shall be levied against the property upon which said fire hazard exists, as a special assessment. The levying of such assessment shall not affect the liability of the person to whom the order is directed to fines and imprisonment as herein provided.
(Code 1999, § 3-705; Code 2011, § 24-26)
905:
The fire chief shall investigate promptly the cause, origin, and circumstance of each and every fire occurring in the city in which property has been destroyed or damaged. If it appears to the officer making investigation that such fire is of suspicious origin, he shall then take immediate charge of the physical evidence and notify the proper authorities designated by law to make the investigation of such matters, and shall further cooperate with them in the collecting of the evidence and in the prosecution of the case.
(Code 1999, § 3-706; Code 2011, § 24-27)
906:
The fire chief shall keep a record of all fires and of all the facts concerning the same, including statistics as to the extent of such fires and the damage caused thereby, and whether such losses were covered by insurance, and if so, in what amount. All such records shall be public.
(Code 1999, § 3-707; Code 2011, § 24-28)
907:
The fire chief shall submit an annual report on the activities under this chapter to the council.
(Code 1999, § 3-708; Code 2011, § 24-29)
910:
The fire chief shall require the officials of public, private, and parochial schools, and other educational institutions to have periodic fire drills, and to keep all doors and exits unlocked during school hours.
(Code 1999, § 3-710; Code 2011, § 24-47)
911:
No person shall at any time place any encumbrances of any kind before or upon any fire escape, balcony or ladder intended as a means of escape from fire. It shall be the duty of every member of the police department who shall discover any fire escape encumbered in any manner to forthwith report the same through his department channels to the police chief, who shall immediately notify the owner or his agent or tenant to remove such encumbrance, and the encumbrance shall thereupon be immediately removed.
(Code 1999, § 3-714; Code 2011, § 24-48)
912:
Every exit in any theater or motion picture house shall be plainly indicated by a sign bearing the word "Exit," which sign shall be kept lit throughout each performance.
(Code 1999, § 3-715; Code 2011, § 24-49)
913:
All doors, aisles, and passageways within and leading into or out of theaters, churches, and all other places of public assemblage shall (during the entire time which any show, performance, service, exhibition, lecture, concert, or other assemblage may be held therein) be kept adequately lit and free from easels, signs, standards, campstools, chairs, sofas, benches, and any other article that might obstruct or delay the exit of the audience, congregation, or assemblage. Doors of such buildings, while occupied, shall not be fastened so that they cannot easily be opened by anyone from within. No person shall sit or stand or remain seated or standing, nor shall the owner or operator of such place allow any person to remain, in any such place of public assemblage in any aisle under any circumstances, or in any exit, or passage required for the safe exit of the assemblage. Clear passage from all exits and on outside sidewalks of all theaters and other places of public assemblage shall be maintained at all times. No aisle, passageway or stairway in any store shall be obstructed with tables, showcases, or other obstructions during the hours such store is open to the public.
(Code 1999, § 3-716; Code 2011, § 24-50)
916:
It shall be unlawful for any person to tamper with any fire alarm except in case of fire, except by authority from the city or its authorized employees.
(Code 2011, § 24-74)
917:
It shall be unlawful for any person to make, give, send, or turn in, in any manner or way whatsoever, a false fire alarm or riot alarm, knowing the same to be false.
(Code 2011, § 24-75)
State Law reference— Similar provision, O.C.G.A. § 16-10-27.
918:
No persons other than those firefighters on official business shall tamper with firefighting equipment either on public or private property.
(Code 2011, § 24-76)
919:
It shall be unlawful for any person to obstruct in any manner any firefighting apparatus or any of the officers or members of the fire department in the performance of their duties. It shall be unlawful for any person to obstruct any fireplug so as to obstruct approaches to the same by the fire department.
(Code 2011, § 24-77)
920:
No persons other than firefighters, city officials, police officers, and the property owner or his agent shall be allowed within the immediate vicinity of a fire, unless such persons are given permission to do so by the fire chief.
(Code 2011, § 24-78)
State Law reference— Refusal to disperse at request of officer or firefighter, O.C.G.A. § 16-10-30.
921:
It shall be unlawful for any person to build, maintain, suffer or permit an extraordinary fire hazard on his premises or on premises occupied or used by him in the construction of buildings, storage of inflammables, explosives, or combustibles, or the use of open flames, etc. The term "extraordinary fire hazard," as used herein, shall be construed to mean any condition that would be manifestly unsafe as a fire hazard or that would greatly increase the probability of fire or the injury of persons by fire. In this connection, the minimum standards promulgated in such cases by the National Board of Fire Underwriters shall be considered as prima facie evidence of such hazard.
(Code 2011, § 24-79)
924:
It shall be unlawful to conduct any type of burn outside of a residence or business without first obtaining permission of the city fire chief and a special burn permit number.
(Code 2011, § 24-102; Ord. No. 06-02, § 1, 2-14-2006; Ord. of 3-9-2021)
925: Editor's note— Ord. of 3-9-2021 repealed § 22-145, which pertained to permits to be issued by fire chief for limited purposes, and derived from Code 2011, § 24-103; Ord. No. 06-02, § 2, 2-14-2006.
926:
(a) The procedure to be followed for violators will be that the police department will be summoned to all fires and will issue a citation for any violations of this article. The fire department will be summoned to all fires and will put out any fires that are deemed to be in violation of this article.
(b) Fines for those persons in violation of this article will be $100.00 for the first offense, $250.00 for the second offense, and $500.00 for the third offense.
(Code 2011, § 24-104; Ord. No. 06-02, §§ 3, 4, 2-14-2006)
927:
It shall be unlawful for any person to permit or suffer rubbish, refuse or articles of a combustible or inflammable nature to accumulate or remain on any lot or premises.
(Code 1999, § 3-717; Code 2011, § 24-105)
928:
No person shall burn or cause to be burned any trash, refuse, shavings, paper, leaves, litter, or other material of any kind outside any commercial building or upon any street, sidewalk, alley, or other public area.
(Code 1999, § 3-711; Code 2011, § 24-106; Ord. of 3-9-2021)
929:
Trash, rubbish, or anything manmade shall not be burned on any private property. Only small hand piles of natural vegetation may be burned with the permission of the Cochran Fire Chief.
(Code 1999, § 3-712; Code 2011, § 24-107; Ord. of 3-9-2021)
930:
No person shall kindle or maintain any bonfire, or shall knowingly furnish the material for any such fire, or authorize any such fire to be kindled or maintained within the limits of the city, unless a written permit to do so shall have first been secured from the fire chief. The term "bonfire" is defined as any fire outside a building not for the purpose of burning trash.
(Code 1999, § 3-713; Code 2011, § 24-108)
931:
All persons that shall burn any tar kiln or pit of charcoal, or set fire to or burn any brush, grass, or other material whereby any property may be endangered or burned, shall keep and maintain a careful and competent watchperson in charge of such kiln, pit, brush or other material while burning. Fire escaping from such kiln, pit, brush or other material while burning shall be prima facie evidence of neglect of these provisions.
(Code 1999, § 3-718; Code 2011, § 24-109)
934:
The fire chief or his designee may issue any written permit required by this article and attach or prescribe conditions or limitations in the issuance thereof. Before issuing a permit, the fire chief or his designee shall inspect and approve the receptacles, vehicles, buildings, appliances, installations, equipment or storage places to be used.
(Code 1999, § 3-709(a); Code 2011, § 24-132)
935:
All applications for permits required by this chapter shall be made to the fire chief or his designee in such form and detail as he shall prescribe. Every such permit shall be for such period as the council shall determine. Permits shall not be transferable and must at all times be kept on the premises designated therein, and shall at all times be subject to inspection by the fire department, police department, fire chief, or his designee.
(Code 1999, § 3-709(b), (c); Code 2011, § 24-133)
937:
One permit only shall be required for retail establishments dealing in, or manufacturing plants using, two or more flammable, combustible, or explosive materials, or keeping the same in the establishment at any one time.
(Code 1999, § 3-709(e); Code 2011, § 24-135)
938:
Permits are required by this article for:
(1) Flammable liquids: storage, handling, and transportation.
(2) Liquefied petroleum gases: handling, transportation, and storage.
(3) Explosives: use, storage, sale, and transportation.
(4) Mechanical refrigeration systems: installation and operation.
(5) Pyrotechnic displays.
(6) Acetylene generators: installation and operation.
(7) Carbide storage.
(8) Public garages: repair and storage.
(9) Tank trucks, tank trailers, tank truck semitrailers: operation.
(10) Paint spray booths: installation and operation.
(11) Small arms ammunition: storage and sale.
(12) Nitrocellulose film: storage.
(13) Pyroxylin plastic: storage and handling.
(14) Tire retreading and rebuilding plants.
(15) Installation of hot plates, ranges, broilers, grease hoods and vents, other than residential.
(Code 1999, § 3-709(f); Code 2011, § 24-136)
943:
(a) The communications center, located in the 9-1-1 facility, shall be operated and maintained by the county through the county sheriff's department. The city has conveyed its interest in certain communications equipment located in the communications center to the county. The sheriff shall be responsible for the employment and supervision of the personnel and efficient operation of the communications center that will continue providing services to both the city and the county on an equal basis.
(b) With regard to the communications center, the county bears responsibility for:
(1) Maintenance, repair, and replacement of needed and necessary equipment as is necessary for the efficient operation of the communications center;
(2) Employment, training, supervision, and pay for necessary communications center personnel in the operation of the communications center;
(3) Providing an adequate place to house the communications center; and
(4) Continuing to provide regular communications services to both the city and the county on an equal basis.
(c) The regular communications services shall include:
(1) County sheriff's department.
(2) City police department.
(3) Fire department.
(4) Civil defense.
(5) Ambulance service.
(6) State patrol.
(7) Game and fish commission.
(8) City utility department.
(9) Forestry unit.
(10) State bureau of investigation.
(11) CB channel nine.
(12) Any other law enforcement agency.
(13) Individual and business fire and burglar alarms, at cost.
(d) The city shall not be responsible for any expenses in connection with the operation and maintenance of said communications center.
(Code 2011, § 24-195)

946:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Fireworks means any combustible or explosive composition or any substance or combination of substances or article prepared for the purpose of producing a visible or audible effect by combustion, explosion, deflagration, or detonation, including blank cartridges, balloons requiring fire underneath to propel them, firecrackers, torpedoes, skyrockets, Roman candles, bombs, sparklers, and other combustibles and explosives of like construction, as well as articles containing any explosive or flammable compound and tablets and other devices containing an explosive substance. The term "fireworks" shall not include model rockets and model rocket engines, designed, sold, and used for the purpose of propelling recoverable aero models; toy pistol paper caps in which the explosive content does not average more than 0.25 grains of explosive mixture per paper cap; or toy pistols, toy cannons, toy canes, toy guns, or other devices using such paper caps; nor shall the term "fireworks" include ammunition consumed by weapons used for sporting and hunting purposes.
(Code 2011, § 24-214; Ord. No. 05-3, § I, 8-9-2005)
947:
Except as otherwise provided by state law, it shall be unlawful for any person or other entity to use, explode, cause to be exploded, possess, manufacture, transport, or store any fireworks within the corporate limits of the city.
(Code 2011, § 24-215; Ord. No. 05-3, § I, 8-9-2005)
State Law reference— Similar provision, O.C.G.A. § 25-10-2; state preemption of local government prohibition and regulation of fireworks sales and use, O.C.G.A. § 36-60-24.
948:
The city police are authorized and directed at any time, at the expense of the owner, to seize, take, or cause to be removed to a place of safety, any stock of fireworks or combustibles possessed, used, displayed, sold, offered or exposed for sale, or held in any manner in violation of this article.
(Code 2011, § 24-216)
State Law reference— Similar provision, O.C.G.A. § 25-10-6.
949:
Footnote 1:
State Law reference— General municipal authority for health and welfare, O.C.G.A. § 36-34-4; county boards of health, O.C.G.A. § 31-3-1 et seq.; smoke free air, O.C.G.A. § 31-12A-1 et seq.; smoking prohibited in local government buildings, O.C.G.A. § 31-12A-2; power of county board of health to adopt and enforce rules and regulations of local application, O.C.G.A. § 31-3-6.
950:
The city adopts the rules and regulations of the county health department as fully as if set forth in full in this chapter. A copy of the county health department rules and regulations shall be available in the office of the city clerk.
(Code 2011, § 26-1)
951:
Any person owning or having possession of a dead animal not intended to be used for food shall immediately bury the same or dispose of such animal as the chief of police may direct.
(Code 2011, § 26-2)
952:
The occupant of any building or dwelling and the owner of any lot shall keep the sidewalks before his respective building or lot clean of refuse and free of the growth of weeds. As used in this section, the term "sidewalks" shall include all the ground, whether paved or not, between the property line and the curbline.
(Code 1999, § 6-607; Code 2011, § 26-3)
953:
It shall be unlawful to commit or do any act which endangers the public health.
(Code 1999, § 6-613; Code 2011, § 26-4)
954:
It shall be unlawful to spit or expectorate on any public sidewalk or other public place or on the floor or walls of any store, theater, hall, public vehicle, or other place frequented by the public or to which the public is invited.
(Code 1999, § 6-616; Code 2011, § 26-5)
955:
Footnote 1:
State Law reference— Law enforcement generally, O.C.G.A. § 35-1-1 et seq.; compensation of law enforcement officers on commission basis prohibited, O.C.G.A. § 36-30-9; dispatch centers to have trained communications officers on staff, O.C.G.A. § 36-26-19.
959:
The police department shall consist of the chief of police and such other officers and personnel. Police department personnel shall be organized according to a paramilitary ranking system common in other police department in the state.
(Code 2011, § 30-19)
960:
Prior to entering upon the duties of their respective offices, all full-time and part-time officers of the police department shall take an oath prescribed by the police department.
(Code 2011, § 30-20)
961:
(a) The police chief shall be a department head who serves as the administrative officer of the police department.
(b) In the exercise of his duties and in coordination with the city manager, the police chief shall have the authority to establish and enforce rules and regulations for the department, which rules shall, however, be consistent with this Code, all other resolutions and ordinances of the city, and the laws of the state.
(Code 2011, § 30-21)
962:
The chief of police shall:
(1) Conduct community public relations and crime prevention programs when required by the city manager.
(2) Issue orders and official administrative rules and regulations to the police officers of the city.
(3) Keep a comprehensive and detailed daily record in permanent form, showing:
a. All known or reported offenses or crimes committed within the corporate limits.
b. All arrests made by police officers.
c. All police investigations made, funerals convoyed, fire calls answered, and other miscellaneous activities of the police department.
(Code 1999, § 3-810; Code 2011, § 30-22)
964:
It is the duty of the officers of the Cochran Police Department to acquire a full knowledge of and to enforce all of the ordinances of the city and in all statutes applicable therein, to become familiar with the rules and regulations established by the Cochran Police Department concerning the discipline, good order, proper conduct, care, and management of the Cochran Police Department, and to respect and obey all orders of the chief of police not in conflict with the law and ordinances of the city.
(Code 2011, § 30-24; Amend. of 9-8-2020)
965:
The chief of police shall be responsible for the compilation and maintenance of the city police department operations manual, a copy of which shall be available to employees of the police department.
(Code 2011, § 30-25)
966:
Police officers of the city may make arrests for violations of this Code, municipal ordinances, and state laws when such violations are committed in their presence or when they have obtained a valid arrest warrant from the judge of the municipal court or from some other proper authority. In exercising such power of arrest, all police officers shall see that all necessary warnings are given to the accused as required by law.
(Code 2011, § 30-26)
967:
Each member of the police department shall be deemed always on duty, subject to relief therefrom as shall be allowed by proper authority, and the same responsibility as to the suppression of disturbances, arrest of offenders and violation of the rules and regulations of the police department shall rest upon them when not in uniform as when in uniform.
(Code 1999, § 3-811; Code 2011, § 30-27)
968:
All police officers, upon employment, shall acquire a full knowledge of all laws, ordinances, rules and regulations of the city, thereby preparing themselves to act intelligently on all occasions where their services are needed. All members of the Cochran Police Department shall also become familiar with the rules and regulations established by the chief of police concerning the discipline, good order, proper conduct, care and management of the Cochran Police Department. Ignorance of such ordinances, rules and regulations shall be no excuse for any breach of any of the same by a Cochran Police Officer.
(Code 1999, § 3-812; Code 2011, § 30-28; Amend. of 9-8-2020)
969:
All police officers shall wear the prescribed uniform and equipment at all times when on duty, unless otherwise ordered by a superior officer. No member of the police department shall go on duty unless he has in his possession and on his person all the necessary equipment to be used by him in the discharge of his duty. Uniforms shall be kept clean and pressed and footwear shall be kept clean and tidy at all times.
(Code 1999, § 3-813; Code 2011, § 30-29)
970:
No police officer, while on duty or in uniform, shall take or drink any intoxicant, including, but not limited to, beer, wine, and other alcoholic beverages. Any officer violating this section shall be subject to immediate dismissal from the department.
(Code 1999, § 3-814; Code 2011, § 30-30)
972:
Cochran Police Department Personnel shall follow the rules and regulations set forth in the city personnel policy handbook and the Cochran Police Department S.O.P.'s.
(Code 1999, § 3-816; Code 2011, § 30-32; Amend. of 9-8-2020)
975:
Disposition of all personal property seized or abandoned and in the custody of the police department shall be disposed of only in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 17-5-54.
(Code 1999, § 3-817; Code 2011, § 30-53)

978:
The city and the county have entered into a mutual aid agreement to provide for additional law enforcement protection for the citizens of each political subdivision during emergency situations by making the most efficient use possible of the law enforcement personnel of both political subdivisions.
